title: Tanla Platforms shares crash 6% - Experts decode future of 'long-term downtrend' | What lies ahead for CPaaS stock? | Stock Market News
text:
Tanla Platforms shares crashed 6% in intraday trading on Monday, 19 October, before paring some losses. Tanla Platforms share price opened at ₹562 against its previous close of ₹560.40 and dropped 5.60% to an intraday low of ₹529, with volume surging 1.57 times. However, it trimmed some losses later and traded 1.67% lower at ₹551 around 12:25 PM.

Tanla Platforms is an AI-native platform company transforming digital interactions by empowering users and enabling enterprises through its innovation-led SaaS solutions.

The stock is up 6% year-to-date compared to a 13% fall in the equity benchmark Sensex. Over the last six months, it is up 12% compared to a 6% decline in the Sensex.

On a monthly scale, Tanla Platforms shares are down over 1% after a 2% rise in the previous month.

The stock hit a 52-week low of ₹372 on 30 March this year after hitting a 52-week high of ₹726.05 on 17 October last year.

According to Aditya Thukral, founder and analyst at AT Research and Risk Managers, Tanla Platforms has been in a long-term downtrend with the formation of lower highs and lower lows. However, after the formation of a low in March 2026, the stock has turned sideways.

"As the stock has moved upwards in a corrective structure, the stock has not completed its downside yet and would revisit the lows of ₹365.90 in the coming months or so. However, from the short- or medium-term perspective, we expect the stock to trade within the territory of ₹480 and ₹656, and either side break would bring a trending move in that direction for a few weeks after that," said Thukral.

"The larger direction still remains on the downside, and any rise towards the resistance of ₹650 is an exit opportunity for longs. However, short-term buying opportunities could exist, but it's advisable to stay away from this stock when one has a long-term perspective," Thukral said.
